description.value: Inlets is the on-site restaurant at West Coast Wilderness Lodge, a remote oceanfront resort nestled in the wilderness near Egmont on BC's Sunshine Coast. The lodge sits at the gateway to Princess Louisa Inlet and the Skookumchuck Rapids, offering a dramatic backdrop for dining. The restaurant is the culinary centrepiece of an all-inclusive wilderness retreat experience that has operated since the late 1990s.

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The website at wcwl.com confirms 'Inlets' is 'Inlets Restaurant,' the dining venue within West Coast Wilderness Lodge at 6649 Maple Road, Egmont, BC. The site provides address and phone not present in OSM tags. No cyclist-specific amenities (bike parking, water, washrooms) are mentioned anywhere on the website; restaurant access appears primarily structured for lodge guests, with Heritage Lodge guests having 'Priority Restaurant Access' and Villas guests having 'Limited Restaurant Access — Inquire for availability,' with no explicit mention of walk-in or public dining.
concerns: Restaurant access appears primarily structured for lodge guests (Heritage Lodge gets 'Priority Restaurant Access'; Villas guests have 'Limited Restaurant Access — Inquire for availability'). It is not confirmed that walk-in or non-guest diners are accepted, which may limit practical utility for passing cyclists.
OSM community classification is 'Vancouver Island & Gulf Islands' but Egmont is on the Sunshine Coast mainland, not Vancouver Island.
OSM name 'Inlets' omits the word 'Restaurant'; full name per website is 'Inlets Restaurant.' No normalization applied per rules.
URL discovery confidence was marked 'medium' in OSM; however, website content clearly corroborates the association of 'Inlets Restaurant' with wcwl.com.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: Real, operating restaurant at a legitimate wilderness lodge; useful to touring cyclists who may be staying at or passing through the Egmont area.
enrichment_extras.notes: The website lists 'Hiking & Biking' under Things To Do, suggesting cyclist-aware staff, but no bike-specific infrastructure for the restaurant itself is described. The 'Fly N' Dine' seaplane dining experience is mentioned in navigation but content was not available to confirm details.
